### 2026-07-22 (later) update — Section 2 RESOLVED, and sub-8-bit precision added

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.policy.later-update-section-2-resolved-and-sub-8-bit/1` · scope `all`

- **Section 2 was a real DWT bug, and this is it.** `forward_97_vertical_in_place` /
  `inverse_97_vertical_in_place` scaled a *one-row* resolution by INV_K / K.
  The pair round-trips through our own encoder, so every test passed, but it
  does not match conformant streams: OpenJPEG returns from both
  `opj_dwt_encode_and_deinterleave_v_real` and `opj_v8dwt_decode` on height 1
  without touching the data, and **our own horizontal 1-D path already treated
  the case as an identity** — the two disagreed. This is exactly the drift §2
  and §5-trap-1 recorded when the decomposition bound was lifted: a codestream
  that signals more levels than its dimensions need passes through several 1x1
  levels, so its DC comes out multiplied by K^n while the AC stays
  pixel-perfect. On the 884x1344 / 17-resolution repro a fit against OpenJPEG
  gave `ours = 1.002 * opj + 194` — a pure DC offset, K^5 = 2.8158.
  With the identity restored the dimension-derived bound has nothing left to
  reject; `max_dwt_decompositions` is gone and the only limit is the spec's own
  `NL <= 32`. Repro (Howard R. Turner, *Science in Medieval Islam* obj7):
  max abs diff 5, mean 0.147, 3062 of 1,188,096 px over 2 — the 9/7 float floor
  at 11 real levels rather than the usual 5, diffuse and edge-concentrated.
  End-to-end 0.2424 silent-blank(codec) -> 0.0014.
- **Sub-8-bit sample precision (1/2/4-bit) is implemented.** The SIZ gate
  accepted only 8..=16 bits; bitonal scans are 1-bit and were the largest
  remaining census class. Nothing in the pipeline needed a special case.
  Verified bit-exact vs OpenJPEG (max abs diff 0) on pdfbox/3246 obj3.
  **NOTE for future verification work:** the CLI's PNG writers used to clamp
  raw samples to 0..255, which wrote a 1-bit page as 0/1 and *clipped* 16-bit
  components instead of scaling them. They now scale by component precision.
- **Renderer-side caveat (not a codec issue):** pdf-renderer widens sub-8-bit
  samples with PDFium's `src << (8 - prec)`, not full-range scaling, because
  that is what PDFium's `CJpx_Decoder::Decode` does and it is what the corpus
  grades against (exactly 0.00000 on pdfbox/3246 and 4326; full-range leaves
  them at 0.81-0.99). Do not "fix" that to match OpenJPEG's writers.

### 4. `TPsot==TNsot` non-conformant tile-parts — ~2 files  [RESOLVED 2026-07-22 — the assembly-bug diagnosis in this section is WRONG; real cause was a missing `inalign` byte-realignment. See the 2026-07-22 update near the top.]

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.policy.tpsot-tnsot-non-conformant-tile-parts-2-files/1` · scope `all`

- **Error:** `tile-part contains data after the tile's packet sequence`
- **Repro:** `Prussian-Line-Infantry-1792-1815.pdf` obj15 (1208×1638, 3-comp,
  csty=0, no precincts). OpenJPEG decodes it, emitting
  `[WARNING] Non conformant codestream TPsot==TNsot.`
- **Reject site:** `src/decode/t2.rs` `push_tile_part` ~line 171-176 — after the
  full packet sequence is read, leftover bytes trigger the error.
- **Diagnosis & TRAP:** the leftover bytes are **not** padding — they are a
  genuine tile-part chunk that our tile-part assembly misplaces because the
  stream sets `TPsot == TNsot` (an off-by-one tile-part index). I tried the
  naive fix (break out of the loop, ignore the tail); it decodes but **corrupts
  a 256-row code-block band** (rows 768-1023 of 1638; measured 1.4% of pixels
  >30 off, a visible stripe). That is a silent mis-decode — worse than the clean
  blank — so the strict failure is kept deliberately (see the NOTE comment now
  in `push_tile_part`).
- **Recommended approach:** fix the **tile-part boundary / ordering** for the
  non-conformant `TPsot==TNsot` case in `src/decode/mod.rs`
  `tile_part_indices_by_tile` (the TNsot-advisory logic) so every tile-part's
  payload is assigned to the correct tile and concatenated in the right order —
  then there is no "trailing" data. Compare against OpenJPEG's tolerant
  tile-part handling (`opj_j2k_read_sot` / the `TPsot==TNsot` warning path).
  Verify the Prussian stream reaches max diff ≤ 2 with no corrupted band.

### 13. GPU path: useful, but only with renderer integration

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.policy.gpu-path-useful-but-only-with-renderer/1` · scope `all`

NVIDIA’s current nvJPEG2000 library offloads every decode stage except Tier-2 to Pascal-or-newer GPUs, supports 5/3 and 9/7, multiple tiles, up to four components, common chroma subsampling, resolution/tile decode, partial decode, RGB output controls, and reusable decode state. ### 2. Degenerate 1-sample DWT split — ~8 files  [RESOLVED 2026-07-22 — root cause was a K/INV_K scaling on a one-row resolution in the *vertical* pass; see the update near the top. The "relaxing the bound drifts" note below is accurate but the cause is now fixed.]

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.requirement.degenerate-1-sample-dwt-split-8-files-resolved/1` · scope `all`

- **Error:** `COD decomposition levels N exceed DWT limit N for image
  dimensions WxH`
- **Repro:** `Neo-Confucianism-in-History.pdf` obj9 — a **176×16** tile
  declaring **5** decomposition levels (numresolutions=6). OpenJPEG decodes it.
- **Reject site:** `src/j2k/decode_markers.rs` `max_dwt_decompositions`
  (~line 577) returns `ceil(log2(min_dim))`; for min_dim=16 that's 4, so 5 is
  rejected at line 462-465.
- **Diagnosis (IMPORTANT — this is a real DWT bug, not just a bound):** the
  extra level splits an axis that is already down to **1 sample** (16 → 8 → 4 →
  2 → 1, then a 5th level on the height axis operates on a 1-sample band). I
  measured that if you merely relax the bound to `ceil(log2(max_dim))` and let
  it decode, `jp2lam`'s **inverse DWT drifts ~16/255 (mean), max 25** vs
  OpenJPEG on that axis — i.e. it silently mis-decodes. So the bound is
  currently kept strict *on purpose* (a clean B3-flagged failure beats a wrong
  image — see §5).
- **Recommended approach:** fix the inverse DWT (`src/dwt/`, `irrev97.rs` /
  `rev53.rs` and the 2D driver `inverse_97_2d_in_place_at`) to correctly handle
  a lifting step on a length-1 (and length-0) axis — it must be a pass-through
  that matches OpenJPEG's `opj_dwt_decode` boundary handling. **Then** relax
  `max_dwt_decompositions` to `ceil(log2(max_dim))` (the larger dimension) and
  re-verify the 176×16 stream is now max diff ≤ 2. Do the DWT fix first; the
  bound relaxation without it re-introduces the drift.
- **Verification:** decode the dumped `failjpx_…decompositionlevels….jp2` and
  diff vs OpenJPEG — must drop from mean ~16 to ≤ ~1.

### 1. Precincts / SOP / EPH — ~10 files (LARGEST remaining class)

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.requirement.precincts-sop-eph-10-files-largest-remaining/1` · scope `all`

- **Error:** `unsupported packet syntax: precinct partitioning, SOP markers,
  and EPH markers are not implemented`
- **Repro:** `The-Conversion-Of-Armenia-To-The-Christian-Faith.pdf` obj8
  (`D:\Pol was right again\…\Armenia…`). OpenJPEG decodes it.
- **Reject site:** `src/j2k/decode_markers.rs` ~line 475 (`validate_decoder_scope`):
  `if cod.uses_precincts || cod.sop_markers || cod.eph_markers { … }`. The COD
  `Scod` bits are already parsed (`uses_precincts`, `sop_markers`, `eph_markers`
  at lines 335-337; `precinct_sizes: Vec<PrecinctSize>` is carried on
  `CodSegment`).
- **Why it's the big one:** the Tier-2 packet iterator in `src/decode/t2.rs`
  currently assumes **P=1** (one precinct per resolution) — `packet_axis_order`
  iterates only (layer, resolution, component). Precincts add a fourth axis: a
  packet exists per (layer, resolution, component, **precinct**), and the number
  of precincts per resolution is derived from the `PPx/PPy` sizes and the
  resolution's coordinates. This is the load-bearing change.
- **Recommended approach:**
  1. In `t2.rs`, generalize the packet odometer to include the precinct index
     as the innermost spatial axis (Annex B.12 order within a resolution).
     Compute per-resolution precinct counts from `precinct_sizes` and the
     tile-component reference grid (Annex B.6): `numprecincts_x =
     ceil(trx1/2^PPx) - floor(trx0/2^PPx)` etc.
  2. Route each packet's code-block contributions to the code-blocks of its
     precinct only (precincts partition each subband into rectangles; a
     code-block belongs to exactly one precinct). Today `band_lookup` maps
     (component,resolution)→bands; you'll need band→precinct→code-block routing.
  3. **SOP** (`0xFF91`, before a packet) and **EPH** (`0xFF92`, after the packet
     header) are optional delimiters — detect and skip them at the right points
     in `push_tile_part` / the packet header reader. They don't change the data,
     only frame it; but if `sop_markers`/`eph_markers` are set you MUST consume
     them or the byte cursor desyncs.
  4. Port against OpenJPEG's `opj_t2_decode_packets` / `opj_pi_*` for the
     iteration order and precinct math — that's the reference the corpus was
     produced against.
- **Verification:** the Armenia streams; expect 9/7 max diff ≤ 2. Add a focused
  unit test with a precinct-partitioned fixture (`opj_compress -c [64,64]` makes
  one). Re-run the census; this should clear ~10 files.

### 2026-07-22 update — Sections 3 and 4 RESOLVED (the §4 diagnosis below was WRONG)

`proposed` · `@lege-ecosystem.requirement.update-sections-3-and-4-resolved-the-4/1` · scope `all`

- **Section 4 was NOT a tile-part assembly bug.** That diagnosis is disproven:
  the Prussian obj15 repro has 35 tiles with an identical 6-part/TNsot=5
  structure, yet only tile 16 failed — an assembly/ordering fault would break
  all 35. The real cause is that the Tier-2 packet-header bit reader
  (`PacketBioReader`) was missing the terminating **byte-realignment** (ISO/IEC
  15444-1 Annex B.10.1 = OpenJPEG `opj_bio_inalign`): when a packet header's
  last consumed byte is `0xFF`, the following bit-stuff byte belongs to the
  header and must be consumed before the body. Tile 16's R3C0 header ends
  `0xFF 0x00`; the old reader sliced the body one byte early at the stuff byte
  and desynced every later packet of that tile — which surfaced as the "leftover
  bytes after the packet sequence" error, and (under naive tail-tolerance) as
  the exact documented 256-row corruption stripe. Fix: `PacketBioReader::inalign()`
  called after every packet-header parse (`src/decode/t2.rs`). Verified: the
  corrupt rows 768-1023 go from max 255 / 75134 px >30 to max 3 / 0 px >30;
  overall max 4 (MCT float floor); end-to-end all pages `degraded=0`.
- **Section 3's named repros were the same `inalign` desync, not truncation.**
  Profit-Over-People obj4 now decodes bit-exact (5/3 max 0); the Imre Nagy
  streams decode within the MCT float floor. **Genuine** stream truncation is
  kept strict — a raw-truncated stream makes OpenJPEG itself error ("Tile part
  length inconsistent with stream length"), so a clean failure is correct there.
- **Also landed 2026-07-22:** 4:2:0 sYCC chroma-subsampling (narrowly gated;
  per-component Annex B.2 geometry + `sycc420_to_rgb`-matching upsample), and
  colr METH 3/4 (any-ICC / vendor colour, inferring the space from the ICC data
  space or component count; ambiguous 2-component rejected cleanly) + palette
  channel-count reconciliation. All verified bit-exact vs OpenJPEG.

## Observations

### jp2lam lossy quality trails JPEG XL/BPG and collapses with resolution (codec-headsup, 2026-08-11)

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.encode-quality.headsup-measurement-2026-08-11/1` · scope `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/dwt/pcrd.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/encode/**"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/plan/**"`

A standalone Rust head-to-head (codec-headsup, at /mnt/Samsung980_1TB/Rust-projects/codec-headsup) compared jp2lam JPEG 2000, libjxl JPEG XL, and bpg-rs BPG on phone photos (a balanced 100x ~50MP + 100x ~12MP sample), grading DECODED RGB with the butteraugli and ssimulacra2 crates. At a fixed operating point (JXL cjxl -d 1.0 -e 9; BPG best qp12; jp2lam RateControl::Quality(98) via Preset::PhotoHigh), across the first 35 completed images jp2lam q98 reached a mean butteraugli of ~4.2 (median ~3.8) versus ~1.3 for JPEG XL and ~1.4 for BPG, while being LARGER than JPEG XL in 34/35 cases (mean size jp2/bpg 0.87, jxl/bpg 0.60, jxl/jp2 0.73).

Quality was strongly resolution-dependent at the SAME quality setting: jp2lam q98 achieved butteraugli ~2 on ~12MP images but ~5-10 on ~50MP images (e.g. 20260105_095336, 50MP: jp2 butteraugli 10.2 at 4.93MB vs jxl butteraugli 1.31 at 4.22MB), and mean ssimulacra2 fell from ~88 on 12MP to ~82 on 50MP. A fixed jp2lam quality therefore does not hold a fixed perceptual quality, and jp2lam's quality-per-byte on this photographic set is below both next-gen codecs. Separately, decoding a 50MP JP2 exceeded the default DecodeLimits working-set cap (estimated ~3.0 GB vs the 1 GiB default), aborting decode until the limit was raised.

### jp2lam encodes an alpha channel as a fourth/second component with a cdef box; ImageMagick cannot oracle translucent colour

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.encode-quality.jp2lam-alpha-channel-20261103/1`

An image with one component more than its colour space has colour channels is encoded with the extra component as straight opacity: coded on its own outside the ICT (the transform and the per-component loaders now cover components 0..3 only), declared in a JP2 cdef box identical byte for byte to the one ImageMagick/OpenJPEG writes ((0,0,1),(1,0,2),(2,0,3),(3,1,0)), and reported by this crate's decoder as in_data_alpha. Lossless RGBA and gray+alpha round-trip exactly; lossy keeps use_mct on the colour planes; layers, tiles, bypass and borrowed views combine with it. Perceptual (SSIMULACRA2) targets reject alpha because the metric scores colour only.

ImageMagick is not usable as an oracle for the colour of translucent pixels: a lossless RGBA JP2 it encodes itself does not round-trip through its rgba: export (4193 of 4234 translucent pixels and all 24 opaque ones differ, identically for our file and its own), while -alpha extract reproduces the alpha plane exactly. The alpha test therefore checks the alpha plane exactly and that OpenJPEG's rgba: export of our file equals its export of ImageMagick's own lossless encode of the same pixels.

### jp2lam encoder-review fixes: decoder 5/3 fallback bug, precinct limit, Lege facade misuse

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.encode-quality.jp2lam-encoder-review-fixes-20261103/1`

Working an external review of jp2lam as a general encoder turned up three defects beyond the review's list. (1) The decoder's checked i128 inverse 5/3 fallback, taken whenever inverse_fast_path_is_safe predicts i32 overflow (9+ decomposition levels on 8-bit data, fewer on 16-bit), used the odd sample's own slot instead of the mirrored even sample at the right edge of even-length lines; streams decoded exactly by OpenJPEG 2.5 (ImageMagick) came back wrong from jp2lam (150x97 at 9 levels: 13454 of 14550 samples). (2) The encoder writes one precinct per subband with PPx=PPy=15, so any tile crossing a multiple of 32768 samples produced packets the precinct partition does not match; such tilings are now rejected and TilePolicy::Auto picks a precinct-sized tile. (3) Lossless RGB never uses the RCT (native_use_mct is 9/7-only), contrary to the review's claim; documented, not changed.

Lege's facade (lege-process/encoding/jp2.rs) discarded every Jp2Settings field but rate, and mapped rate through 100/sqrt(rate), which for every ratio above 4 landed on the q50 floor; encode_to_target_size ran a seven-encode quality ladder instead of RateControl::TargetBytes; the display path fell back on any error. Production page/region images already used the verified display path and MRC backgrounds the ApproxQuality preset, which is now spelled out as RateControl::ApproxQuality rather than left to EncodeOptions::quality.

Open, not attempted: multiple quality layers, Tier-1 mode switches (bypass/termall/segsym exist only under cfg(test) and the packet writer assumes one terminated segment), alpha/cdef, palettes, resolution boxes, a 10-16-bit perceptual metric, and the resolution-dependent ApproxQuality lambda scaling.

### jp2lam gained quality layers and the six code-block coding switches; both verified against OpenJPEG

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.encode-quality.jp2lam-layers-and-code-block-styles-20261103/1`

Quality layers (CodingOptions::layers): the final layer is the rate control's own selection and each lower layer is PCRD rerun on measured-MSE curves truncated at the final pass counts, so layers nest and the decoded picture equals the single-layer one; only packet headers are added (83 bytes on a 256x192 Count(4) encode). OpenJPEG decoded that file layer by layer at 17.9, 20.9, 28.0 and 38.5 dB. Single-layer output stayed byte-identical across nine configurations. The first attempt failed on multi-block bands because inclusion tag-tree values were set per block during coding; a parent node's value must be final before its first leaf is coded, so all first inclusions of a band are now set before any block's header bits.

Code-block style (CodingOptions::code_block_style): all six Annex D switches are written to COD and honoured by the encoder, which took a general per-pass loop (the all-off style keeps the tuned single-segment path, byte-identical). The decoder gained raw-segment decoding and Table D.9 segmentation, so bypass streams no longer fail. Twelve style combinations round-trip exactly lossless, within 2 of OpenJPEG lossy, and with layers plus tiles. Two decoder decisions: a segmentation-symbol mismatch on the last pass a stream carries is tolerated, because a rate-truncated codeword loses its marker first; and the ERTERM flush keeps the reference accounting (the byte at the write position is excluded, matching RefMq), since including it changed decoded symbols.

Open: OpenJPEG prints "PTERM check failure: N synthetized 0xFF markers" for predictable-termination streams that PCRD truncated mid-codeword (21 warnings across the lossy style sweep, none on lossless or layered-lossless). Truncating only at terminated passes when predictable_termination is set would remove it at some rate cost; not done. Lege's Jp2Settings has no field for the style, so Lege cannot select it yet.

### No Lege crate depends on a sibling checkout: jpxl-perceptual from crates.io, liminalkit from GitHub

### jp2lam encode writes one fixed Part 1 coding recipe

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.jp2lam.encoder-codestream-recipe/1` · scope `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/j2k/markers.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/plan/**"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/tiling.rs"`, `path "lege-process/encoding/jp2.rs"`

The production encoder does not expose Part 1 coding parameters. encode_cod writes Scod 0, LRCP only (ProgressionOrder has no other variant), one quality layer, code-block style 0, and either reversible 5/3 or irreversible 9/7. Decomposition count is chosen internally and capped at 5 for gray and 6 for sRGB. Code-block size is 32×32 below quality 30 and 64×64 otherwise. Guard bits are 2. Image and tile origins are 0. Each tile is exactly one tile-part. Precinct index is always 0 (one precinct per subband). Rsiz is 0. Tier-1 can encode arithmetic bypass, predictable termination, and segmentation symbols, but the plan never selects them and the COD marker would not signal them. There is no TLM, PLT, SOP, EPH, ROI, or progression-order change. Lege's Jp2Settings still carries num_resolutions, prog_order, irreversible, tile_size, codeblock, rates, and psnrs; encode() ignores them except to map rate, or the last rates/psnrs entry, onto a single quality number.

### jp2lam encode accepts only unsigned 8–16-bit gray and sRGB

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.jp2lam.encoder-color-and-sample-limits/1` · scope `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/jp2.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/model.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/plan/**"`

Encoder validation accepts only unsigned samples at precision 8..=16 with dx=dy=1, and only gray or sRGB. Signed samples, chroma subsampling, and any other precision are rejected. EncodingPlan::build_view rejects CMYK as decode-only and rejects YUV/YCbCr. Three-component input always applies the multiple-component transform; there is no way to store components unchanged. There is no alpha, palette, or extra-component colorspace. The JP2 writer emits the signature, file type, image header, optional per-component bit depth, one color-spec box, and the codestream. It does not write a channel definition, palette, component mapping, capture/display resolution, or XML/UUID box. The decoder already accepts CMYK, cdef opacity, and palettes, so those are encode gaps rather than format gaps.

### jp2lam content profiles are global; text-versus-photo block classes are unwired

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.jp2lam.encoder-content-allocation/1` · scope `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/encode/backend/native/**"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/perceptual/**"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/profile.rs"`

ContentProfile::Document is one global quantizer curve tuned for cleaned text pages. Photo and General share the photographic curve. The live code-block classifier is classify_from_nonzero_fraction and only produces Flat, Gradient, or TexturePhoto. EdgeText and BackgroundNoise exist only under cfg(test). Taubman subband masking is cfg(test); the live rate path passes a neutral weight. The luma contrast mask runs for enumerated gray and sRGB and is skipped for an RGB ICC profile. A mixed page is not split inside the encoder; spatial text-versus-photo allocation has to happen before encode.

### jp2lam quality field is ApproxQuality; the verified floor is a separate control

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.jp2lam.encoder-quality-controls/1` · scope `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/dwt/pcrd.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/encode/**"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/model.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/plan/**"`

When EncodeOptions.rate_control is absent and quality is below 100, resolve_rate_control selects RateControl::ApproxQuality. That ladder's lambda is scaled by (pixels/12e6)^0.35 and is not a SSIMULACRA2 floor. RateControl::Quality is the verified ssimulacra2-jpxl-1 floor and accepts only 8-bit unsigned gray or enumerated sRGB. A Quality or Perceptual target whose source is under 8px on either side silently becomes lossless. RateControl::Quality { level: 100 } returns InvalidInput; a Perceptual score of 100 returns PerceptualTargetMissed with achieved 0. Exact byte, bits-per-pixel, and ratio targets stay on measured MSE; select_stored_tile_passes does not apply perceptual weighting to them. EncodeOptions::photo, photo_quality, display_photo, and the photographic presets set TilePolicy::Auto, and with max_working_memory unset that tiles at 2048. encode_with_psnr scores only gray and sRGB. Perceptual weighting is also off for qualities 96–99.

### jp2lam restricted ICC validation checks the header only

ColorEncoding::restricted_icc and validate_restricted_icc accept a profile whose length matches the header, whose signature is acsp, whose PCS is XYZ, and whose data color space is GRAY or RGB. They do not check profile class or that the profile is a matrix/TRC restricted profile. A LUT-based RGB profile with that header is embedded unchanged, and the encoder does not convert the samples. ### jp2lam max_threads, JP2 box length, and the dead perceptual error

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.jp2lam.encoder-runtime-edges/1` · scope `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/encode/**"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/error.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/jp2.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/model.rs"`

ResourceLimits.max_threads does not size a Rayon pool. Some(1) only disables component-level parallelism; DWT and Tier-1 still use the process pool, and any other Some(n) does nothing unless max_working_memory is also large enough for that component path. JP2 box length is a u32, so wrap_codestream fails in box_len when the container would pass 4 GiB; a raw codestream does not have that limit. Jp2LamError::PerceptualNotImplemented remains a public variant and is never returned. Lossy precision 10–16 is accepted by the planner and quantizer; tests/lossless_roundtrip.rs covers those depths on the reversible path, and the integration tests do not cover a lossy 10–16-bit encode.

### Which Lege JP2 paths use the verified floor and which use ApproxQuality

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.jp2lam.lege-jp2-call-sites/1` · scope `path "lege-process/encoding/jp2.rs"`, `path "lege-process/encoding/streamline.rs"`, `path "lege-process/pipeline/helper_functions.rs"`, `path "lege-process/pipeline/pdf_tokio_pipeline.rs"`, `path "lege-process/pipeline/quality_policy.rs"`

Reader-visible JP2 takes EncodingSettings::Jp2Display: figure regions, covers, full-page color, and gray figure overlays call encode_display, which builds EncodeOptions::display_photo (a PerceptualTarget measured at the display box). The legacy quality number is stored as fallback_quality. encode_display turns every Err, including PerceptualTargetMissed, into encode_image. encode_image sets EncodeOptions.quality and leaves rate_control unset, so that fallback is ApproxQuality at source size, on ContentProfile::General. MRC gray backgrounds call encode_gray_document at mrc_bg_quality (default 55): Document profile plus the quality field, which is ApproxQuality. Preservation color backgrounds call encode_rgb with that same quality number: General profile plus ApproxQuality. The preserved-mask original background calls encode_region_image_sync with display_box None, and jp2_region_settings then selects EncodingSettings::Jp2Lam { quality }. pdf_to_png encodes both ladders only as a debug comparison. quality_policy.rs says the legacy preset survives only as that fallback and that every JP2 site takes the verified path.

### A bitonal DjVu page spends most of its encode time on an all-white IW44 background, not on JB2

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.observation.a-bitonal-djvu-page-costs-more-in-iw44-than-in-jb2/1` · scope `path "lege-codecs/djvulibrust/src/doc/page_encoder.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/djvulibrust/src/encode/iw44/**"`

PageComponents::encode emits an IW44 BG44 background layer for every JB2 page, including a page whose background is entirely white. At A4 and 300 dpi that layer was 466 ms of a 540 ms page, against 19 ms for the JB2 symbol coder itself. Optimizing the IW44 coefficient coder is therefore what actually speeds up Lege's document pages, and the JB2 path is not the bottleneck it looks like. Two follow-ups this exposes: bg_subsample defaults to 1 in this crate while DjVuLibre's c44 defaults to 3, which would cut that blank layer roughly ninefold but changes output and is a policy call; and shapes_to_encoder_format emits one shape per component with every parent -1, so the automatic path never produces MATCHED_COPY or REFINE -- compression left on the table rather than a speed problem.

### PP-OCRv6 on wgpu was blocked by four concrete gaps, all now closed

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.observation.ppocrv6-wgpu-blockers-resolved-20260822/2` · scope `path "lege-gpu/**"`, `path "lege-ocr/**"`, `path "lege-process/scripts/**"`

The earlier finding that a Paddle/WGPU v6 model pack "failed detector construction" had four independent causes, each now fixed. (1) Stock Paddle exports name the graph input `x`, which match_target in lege-gpu/src/vision/onnx/load.rs bound to the paddle-rotate target's fixed 224x224 contract; the v5 assets had been renamed to pp_det_image/pp_rec_image out of band and that recipe was never committed. (2) lege-gpu had no Erf kernel (v6 builds GELU from it, 13x in det, 10-13x in rec); added as UnaryKind::Erf with an Abramowitz-Stegun 7.1.26 WGSL shader and a matching CPU reference. (3) v6 det uses ConvTranspose 2x2/stride-2 and v6 rec keeps BatchNormalization behind a Squeeze; both are rewritten at prep time, ConvTranspose into Conv1x1+DepthToSpace (exact for kernel==stride, zero pad) and BN into Mul+Add. (4) MaxPool/AveragePool rejected auto_pad!=NOTSET and ignored it during shape inference, so PP-OCRv6's stride-1 SAME_UPPER 2x2 windows shrank the feature map by one pixel and surfaced as a Concat axis-2 mismatch; both now resolve auto_pad exactly as Conv already did. Whole-spatial ReduceMean(axes=[2,3]) is also rewritten to GlobalAveragePool at prep. The v6 small dictionary (18708 glyphs) is a near-superset of v5's 18383 - 35 dropped, 360 added - and repairs v5's Latin-1 coverage, which held only 70 of 192 codepoints in U+00C0..U+017F.

### Truetyping's shared glyph dictionary serialized every page's matching behind one mutex, and that lock was the whole critical path

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.observation.truetyping-dictionary-lock-serialized-every-page/2` · scope `path "lege-process/encoding/glyphfont.rs"`

On the 886-page archive.org scan crusadeswholesto0000lamb_1.pdf (RGB JPEG pages, traced at 2400 px), truetyping took 17.4 s for 41 pages and 72.8 s for 201 pages where CCITT4 took 5.1 s for the same 41 pages and 35.3 s for the whole book. Rendering (1.7 s total) and binarization were not the cost. GlyphFontSession::process_page_pixels matched a page's 5000 components against the document dictionary while holding the dictionary mutex, single-threaded; the strict search alone was 38 s of the 73 s wall on 201 pages, and the per-instance cost grew with the dictionary (273 candidates per instance at 41 pages, 400 at 200). The four page workers spent most of their time waiting for the lock. Fix: the per-component search is a read-only parallel probe (rayon, one Comparator per thread) and only folding the answers (votes, refreshes, inserts) runs in sequence; a miss is re-searched only among the prototypes the page changed; the end-of-document alias passes probe in parallel the same way; banks finalize concurrently; the bucket index uses a multiplicative hasher. After: 41 pages 8.5 s, 201 pages 25.9 s, the whole book 2 min 0 s, with per-page glyph extraction flat at 143 to 168 ms across the book (98 s of pages, 19 s of finalize, font build and write for 22 font banks). A 65533-id bank fills in roughly 40 pages of this book: 41 pages made 13691 distinct shapes but 41794 glyph ids (13471 position variants, 4307 compounds, 8529 text variants), so the full book carries 22 fonts totalling 41 MB of a 45 MB output; glyph-id consumption by variants, not matching speed, is now the format's largest cost on long books.

### Truetyping letters off their baseline came from rises measured against a tilted fit but drawn level, and from OCR text identities handing an occurrence another position variant's id

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.observation.truetyping-text-identity-moved-letters-off-their-baseline/2` · scope `path "lege-process/core/pdf_artifact.rs"`, `path "lege-process/encoding/glyphfont.rs"`

Two separate causes, both found on page 51 of crusadeswholesto0000lamb_1.pdf and both fixed in glyphfont.rs. (1) group_lines measured each glyph's rise against the Theil-Sen baseline under that glyph while pdf_artifact draws the whole line level at the fit's midpoint value, so on a tilted line, or any line whose fit a stray shape had tilted, glyphs at the ends were drawn off their ink by slope times distance from the midpoint: the runs of letters at line ends riding high or low. Rises are now measured from the one level height the line is drawn at, so position variants are exact by construction. (2) GlyphDictionary::text_identity kept, per shape, the glyph id that first carried a recognized text, and record_text remapped every later occurrence read as that text onto that id, even when the occurrence was a different position variant of the shape at a different baseline offset. Which variant claimed the text first depended on page order, so the same book showed different letters displaced from run to run (the o in every of three pixels low in one run, mont in Clermont raised in another). Primary-text occurrences now keep their own ids and a secondary text gets a text variant of exactly the occurrence's glyph; the regression test text_identities_keep_each_occurrence_at_its_own_baseline_offset covers both readings.

### Minified stencil /Mask now coverage-averaged: Lege 72 DPI agreement 79.3% -> 97.5%, cost 4-8% on MRC stencil books

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.renderer-headsup.minified-stencil-coverage-20261106/1`

Lege's 72 DPI disagreements on chinese-medicine (242 pages) and centralparktest-repair (94) came from MRC pages whose JPX foreground is cut out by a hard 1-bit stencil /Mask (ABBYY/LuraDocument shape). Lege point-sampled that mask all-or-nothing even when it was shrunk ~4x. The result was aliased text with dropped thin strokes, while PDFium, MuPDF and Hayro average the mask's coverage. Fix (working tree on top of 13109aed, uncommitted at observation): `PreparedImage::minified_stencil_as_coverage` (pdf-render-cpu/src/image.rs), called at the top of `paint_image` (exec.rs), re-expresses a 1-bit stencil that the draw minifies as the equivalent 1-bit /SMask, with polarity carried by /Decode ([1 0] by default, [0 1] for an inverted stencil). Draws that do not minify the mask are unchanged. Pool7 majority agreement at 72 DPI: Lege 79.3% -> 97.5%; it is unchanged at 100% at 144 DPI. Remaining 72 DPI disagreements: 44 Structures pages, where Lege agrees with Hayro, zpdf and MuPDF and differs only from PDFium/pdf-render by 5-7% gross, a filter-phase difference that Hayro shares; and 3 vogtle vector-text pages with a slight antialiasing tone difference (Lege's mean is within 0.1 grey level of MuPDF's). Cost, interleaved A/B of a HEAD worktree build against the fix, 5 reps, P-core pinned: chinese-medicine 0.95-0.96x, centralpark 0.92-0.93x, Structures (soft-mask control) 0.98-0.99x. Unit test `minified_stencil_averages_coverage`; pdf-render-cpu tests pass. Data: .agent/scratch/pdf-render-headsup-20261106/{accuracy/pool7, accuracy/pool7-prefix, ab-fix.log}.

### Round 4 follow-ups: scheduler window, font dedup, adaptive flattening, masked alpha pass, low-bit-depth image path; halftone/HENSKIP tested

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.renderer-headsup.round4-followups-20261104/1`

Round 4 (2026-11-04, main checkout, no worktrees or implementation subagents, no version change; commit e7d1b298eba07cac3f8da5ea8a0ba0514f7cdf54) took the
round-3 "next levers" one at a time. (1) Short-document ramp: the scheduler's fixed reorder window of 12 starved the render
workers on short documents; the default is now reorder_window_for(compile, render) = 4 slots per worker, floor 12, with the
page feed sized to it, and the document font cache resolves each font once across compile workers (per-font slot with an
in-flight lock). vogtle at 8 workers: 0.62x -> level with hayro (best of three 45 -> 38 ms vs 39). (2) Glyph-cache misses:
outline curves are flattened adaptively (fewest uniform segments within 1/16 px, FreeType's threshold, cap 64) instead of a
fixed 8 per curve; beans serial 72 DPI 22.7 -> 14.7 ms (0.77x -> 1.31x hayro). This is the one output change: 2-7% of text
pixels move by 4 levels on average, max 28; PDF_RENDERER_OUTLINE_SEGMENTS=8 reproduces the old output byte for byte and the
corpus hash check runs under it (3698/3698 vs 035660da). (3) Masked area-min alpha pass skips clear runs: Structures' masked
draw 7.7 -> 7.3 ms per page, exact; the AVX2 horizontal pass from the hand-off profiled at 2% and was not built. (4) JBIG2
halftone, tested not changed: a halftone-region PDF made with Lege 1.5.1 (--halftone --text-format jbig2, viaduct; HENSKIP=0,
Lege's encoder never sets it) and synthetic HENSKIP=1 streams all decode identically to hayro; the one defect was in
jbig2enc-rust's test-only stream writer, which fed skipped cells' values into later contexts (T.88 6.2.5.7 has 0), fixed
in tests/common/writer.rs; the decoder is unchanged. (5) Found by that test: 1-, 2- and 4-bit single-component images drawn
axis-aligned at or above their resolution (Lege's own JBIG2/CCITT pages) had no fast path and took the generic per-pixel
loop at ~30 ns a pixel; the new lookup-table nearest painter is byte-identical (unit test; 3740/3740 hashes vs the
pre-change adapter) and brings Lege's own output from 105 to 5.5 ms per page at 144 DPI (hayro 8.3) and 27.5 to 1.9 ms at

### Nov-04 renderer head-to-head timing variance explained: protocol change plus JPX full-resolution decode

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.renderer-headsup.timing-variance-20261104/1`

The 2026-11-04 renderer head-to-head timings differ from the July/August pdfium-diff bench results for three
methodological reasons and one real engine cost. (1) July measured Lege on 20 threads with nested JPX/image-row
parallelism in a pre-warmed process against single-threaded PDFium; November is 8-vs-8 with nested parallelism
off, cold processes, and PDFium in 8 processes (5.7x its serial rate). (2) The serial dump pass ran Lege with
PDF_RENDERER_JPX_CONCURRENCY=1 (unrecognised = Budgeted(8)) while timing used serial: 92 vs 195 ms/page on
chinese-medicine 72 DPI. (3) No CPU affinity on the i7-13700H: pinned P-cores 178-181 ms/page, E-cores 293,
and one unpinned full run landed at 315; single-pass serial numbers carry a 1.6x error bar. Cold start adds
130-480 ms (system font directory scan of 535 files plus first-page caches), which is the whole result for the
3-page documents. (4) The real cost: on the JPX/MRC books the renderer is 13-23 ms/page warm but jp2lam decodes
both full-page JPX layers at full resolution at 144 DPI (SUPERSAMPLE_HEADROOM=2 in pdf-render-cpu prepared.rs
rejects the one-level reduction), 300-380 ms per layer serial; Lege peaks at ~11 pages/s with the whole machine
vs PDFium 30 pages/s with 8 processes. Report and raw data:
.agent/scratch/pdf-render-headsup-20261104/variance-investigation.md and variance-investigation/.

A TensorRT-inclusive package is host-proven but not yet general tester-ready: the runtime is experimental, the current worker is built for CUDA architecture 89, its observed non-system static import closure is 424.58 MiB before models and the Rust CLI, cold engine creation takes about ten minutes on the measured host, and no clean-machine packaged-runtime test or distributable manifest exists. ### Rasterizing truetyping's fitted glyph outlines into a JBIG2 text layer is feasible with existing pieces and would give regular glyphs at JBIG2 size

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.assessment.glyph-outlines-rasterized-into-a-jbig2-layer/1` · scope `path "lege-process/encoding/glyphfont.rs"`, `path "lege-process/encoding/vectorize.rs"`

Every piece exists: PageAnalysis/GlyphDictionary give per-page placements of majority-voted prototypes at the 2400 px working height, vectorize fits quadratic curves to 0.6 px and rasterize (nonzero winding, pixel-centre sampling) already draws them back, and encode_base_layer takes any bilevel page. A new text-layer option would, per page, paint each placed prototype's fitted outline at output scale (1200-1600 px) onto a white page at positions snapped to the output grid, add the page residual downsampled from the binarized page, and hand the result to the JBIG2 symbol encoder; identical rasters per prototype make the symbol classifier's job exact, so dictionaries shrink. Costs: glyph analysis 140-170 ms/page on top of JBIG2, a scanline rasterizer with area coverage for the downscale (rasterize samples centres only), and no font, so the 65533-id bank limit disappears. The edges are regular rather than smooth: a bilevel layer at device resolution cannot carry antialiasing; the smoothness truetyping shows comes from the reader rendering outlines. Not a size win over plain JBIG2 on clean pages; a quality and consistency win on noisy scans. Not implemented as of 2026-09-06.

### jp2lam photographic quality limited by MSE-only, disabled-perceptual, size-matched rate control

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.encode-quality.root-cause/1` · scope `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/dwt/pcrd.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/encode/backend/native/rate.rs"`, `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/src/plan/**"`

jp2lam's lossy photographic quality trails JPEG XL/BPG for structural reasons in the rate-control path, not a coding-correctness bug. The active PCRD selection optimizes measured mean-squared error with no perceptual weighting; the perceptual machinery that exists is disconnected/rolled back; and the quality-to-lambda mapping is calibrated to reproduce old FILE SIZES from one 12MP image, with a resolution term that actively degrades large images. These compound into the measured resolution-dependent quality collapse.

- `#mse-not-perceptual` — The active rate path (src/encode/backend/native/rate.rs raw_records_for_passes) builds RD curves from a measured Annex-J delta-MSE (pass.mse_numerator * quant_step^2 * subband synthesis norm * component weight) and select_for_quality picks passes at an MSE-domain lambda. curves_from_tier1_layout explicitly discards the perceptual inputs (`let _ = (quality, contrast_mask, taubman_weights);`), so selection is MSE-optimal with zero perceptual weighting. butteraugli and ssimulacra2 penalize MSE-optimal allocation, so the codec is optimizing the wrong objective for photographic quality.
- `#perceptual-path-disabled` — A perceptual model exists but is not wired into selection: src/perceptual/ (contrast_mask.rs, taubman_masking.rs), and pcrd.rs functions apply_contrast_masking_to_delta and band_distortion_bias, plus the Taubman2000 distortion model, are present yet unused by the active curves_from_tier1_layout path. rate.rs documents that the real Annex-J delta-MSE + perceptual weighting effort (P1.3) was ROLLED BACK 'pending lambda recalibration'. So the perceptual rate control is stubbed, not merely missing.
- `#resolution-lambda-backwards` — pcrd.rs quality_to_lambda multiplies the RD threshold by resolution_factor = (pixel_count / 12_000_000)^0.35, ~1.65x at 50MP. A higher lambda truncates MORE coding passes, so the largest, most detailed images are quantized/truncated hardest - the opposite of holding constant visual quality. This directly explains the measured 12MP->50MP butteraugli collapse (butteraugli ~2 -> ~5-10 at q98).
- `#size-matched-single-image-calibration` — The whole quality curve is calibrated to REPRODUCE FILE SIZE, not perceptual quality: quality_to_lambda anchors were 'bisected on lear.png' (a single 12MP image) 'so each quality reproduces the file size of the previous heuristic-model curve within ~1%', and plan/derive.rs quality_step_scaler / document_step_scale were tuned on 300-dpi text pages. There is no butteraugli/ssimulacra2-anchored calibration and no cross-resolution or multi-image validation.
- `#uniform-quantization-no-csf` — plan/derive.rs apply_quality_step_scaling multiplies every subband's ISO expounded step by a single quality-only scalar (quality_step_scaler), with no CSF/visual frequency weighting per subband. Bit emphasis across subbands is thus content- and perception-blind before PCRD, and the only band shaping (band_distortion_bias LL 1.2 / HH 0.82) lives in the unused perceptual path.

**supported_by** `@lege-ecosystem.encode-quality.headsup-measurement-2026-08-11/1`

### Lege photographs use the verified floor; ApproxQuality remains on backgrounds and on encode failure

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.jp2lam.lege-approxquality-is-a-fallback-and-a-background-path/1` · scope `path "lege-process/encoding/jp2.rs"`, `path "lege-process/pipeline/pdf_tokio_pipeline.rs"`, `path "lege-process/pipeline/quality_policy.rs"`

Lege is not encoding reader-visible photographs with ApproxQuality. Figure regions, covers, full-page color, and gray figure overlays call EncodeOptions::display_photo, and the legacy quality number is only fallback_quality. That fallback is a defect: encode_display maps every error, including a missed SSIMULACRA2 floor, to a successful ApproxQuality encode at source size, so a file can miss the floor the caller asked for. The MRC gray background staying on Document profile plus the quality field matches the jp2lam decision that document layers stay off the SSIMULACRA2 scale; that layer is a near-white antialias residual, and a score floor would be the wrong objective. The preservation color background (encode_rgb at mrc_bg_quality) and the preserved-mask original background (display_box None) still encode continuous-tone page images with ApproxQuality. quality_policy.rs says every JP2 site takes the verified path; those two backgrounds do not. That is a real quality defect on those paths, and it is a deliberate call site, not jp2lam selecting the wrong ladder by itself.

### Fused-pack SIMD is performance-neutral (memory/codegen-bound)

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.assessment.fused-pack-simd-neutral/1`

Hypothesis from the 2026-08-06 decode flamegraph: the ~15% of cycles in
the scalar fused pack (finalize_centered_f32_u8 + <f32>::clamp +
ict_rgb_f32 + store_rgb_layout inside fuse_pack_f32_into) could be cut
with an 8-wide wide::f32x8 finalize/ICT. Implemented a bit-exact
f32x8 path for the tight parallel branch (output hash unchanged at
c1698aa01d9a325e; 339 lib tests pass). Interleaved A/B on lear q75 RGB
(4 P-core workers, two prebuilt binaries alternated to cancel thermal
drift) showed no difference: baseline 278.3-281.4 ms vs SIMD
278.5-281.3 ms. The "after" flamegraph cycle shares for finalize/clamp
were unchanged, indicating LLVM already auto-vectorizes the scalar
per-pixel loop under fat LTO, and the pack is memory-bandwidth-bound
(reads 3x ~37 MP f32 planes, writes ~37 MP x3 bytes). The change was
reverted as neutral-but-more-complex. Transferable lesson (from
jpegXL-rs): do layout/memory-traffic work before ISA SIMD; SIMD only
accelerates arithmetic between large allocations and copies.
Next real targets by the flamegraph: 9/7 inverse DWT vertical memory
traffic (apply_lift_wide 14% + band gather/scatter memcpy) and Tier-1
MQ/flag hot loop, not the pack arithmetic.

### Renderer and jp2lam memory-efficiency audit, 2026-08-25

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.assessment.renderer-jp2-memory-audit-2026-08-25/1` · scope `path "lege-codecs/jp2lam/**"`, `path "lege-pdf/render/**"`

A static audit found hard-bound and concurrency defects in renderer image caching, unbudgeted decode memory, redundant full-buffer ownership conversions, and three JP2 structural allocation paths capable of materially exceeding current working-memory expectations.

- `#codec-stream-payload-copies` — Codec-first PDF stream compilation materializes the payload as Vec<u8> and then converts it to Arc<[u8]>, causing a second full-payload allocation and copy before decoding.
- `#codestream-structural-metadata` — JP2 codestream parsing retains uncapped marker and tile-part framing vectors before semantic resource validation, allowing compact hostile input to amplify structural metadata allocations.
- `#decoded-image-cache-bound` — The renderer decoded-image cache is not a hard 96 MiB bound: eviction retains one oversized entry per shard, alpha storage is omitted from the charge, and concurrent misses for one key are not coalesced.
- `#narrow-irreversible-scratch` — The 9/7 vertical band scratch allocates 128 columns even when the active component is narrower, allowing a one-column image to allocate 128 times the necessary band scratch and exceed the coarse working-memory estimate.
- `#nested-codec-pools` — Per-render-thread JP2 sessions retain separate dynamically resized Rayon pools; under concurrent rendering this can oversubscribe threads and multiply thread stacks and worker scratch.
- `#palette-allocation-amplification` — JP2 palette parsing allocates all PCLR columns and deep-clones each CMAP-selected column before output-channel validation, allowing repeated mappings to amplify memory and causing ordinary packed palette decode to retain avoidable full i32 planes.
- `#renderer-vec-to-arc-conversions` — Several large renderer conversion paths, including JPX alpha splitting and native-planar fallback, fill Vec<u8> and then convert to Arc<[u8]>, causing avoidable full-output copies and higher transient peaks.
- `#scheduler-decode-accounting` — Renderer scheduler admission accounts for the page surface and transparency-group estimate but not decoded image payloads or JP2 working planes, so concurrent cold image pages can multiply unbudgeted memory.

## Evidence

### Third Opus subagent. Low-target oracle re-sweep (7 x 0.8 MP, body fractions down to 0.05, targets 60-80, 245 new probes) closed the censored-crossing gap: prior_body_fraction refit with a quadratic ln(loss) term, per-target bias at 60/70 went from -16%/-9% to ~0, pooled sd ln 0.175 -> 0.165. Cheapest rung at 60/65/70 is within 1-5% across q50-q90 so outer_rungs_for_target unchanged. Probes on 7 photos x 70-90 x Fast/Balanced: 2.486 -> 2.386 (Fast 2.00, Balanced 2.77), zero misses. Display-floor corpus (11 photos x floors 60-80 x plain/eink400x300/eink600x450/tablet800x600, 220 cells): on 0.8 MP, floor 70 eink 600x450 costs 0.49x plain q75 Fast bytes and delivers 75.6 at display size (source-resolution score 51); eink 400x300 floor 70 = 0.33x (source-res 32); tablet 800x600 floor 70 = 0.64x (source-res 62). 4-6 MP sources into 400x300: 0.08-0.13x with source-resolution scores near or below zero. Display targets: 17.6% accept the first probe, rest 2 probes, 6/165 needed a rescue. Found and fixed 6 hard PerceptualTargetMissed failures: the display metric is non-monotone in body bytes at heavy downscale, so the single correction could land infeasible; backend now adds one rescue probe at the rung ceiling (honest SaturatedTop if it misses). Rescue streams are fat (1.2-4.4 MB) because display_prior_scale is fitted at 0.8 MP only; a 4-6 MP display-crossing sweep would supply the source-size term (ponytail comment). Recommendation recorded in for_quality/for_display docs: default e-ink floor 70 (byte cost per point turns over between 65 and 75), same floor for tablet since the larger panel is already stricter. New examples: perceptual_display.rs, perceptual_probes.rs; perceptual_oracle gained --fractions. Combined-tree gates: lib 381/381 serial, all integration targets, CLI 12/12, fmt clean.

### Two Opus subagents. ### Opus subagent, probe usage. First-probe predictor prior_body_fraction gained per-source terms available for free in the search: near-zero coefficient fraction of the unquantized DWT (computed from the cache, or per-tile recompute on the memory-capped path so the cache stays winner-invariant) and ln(body bytes/pixel); leave-one-source-out sd ln 0.186 -> 0.115 over 12 sources. First probe now aims at floor+reserve. display_prior_scale refit on 112 converged display crossings: ln scale = -4.4888 + 0.5234 ln(display px) - 0.2009 ln(source px) + 0.15, clamped [ratio,1] (fitted on 9 groups sd 0.19; two soft large sources sit ~10x lower, residual sd 0.75 over all 11, documented). Balanced reserve 0.03 -> 0.045 (-0.63 probes for +0.5% bytes); Fast keeps reserve 0.06 with a 3x accept band (JPXL good-enough band). Results 7 x 0.8 MP x floors 70-90: Fast 2.00 -> 1.43 probes (+1.5% bytes, 77% one-probe), Balanced 2.77 -> 1.91 (+0.5%, 49% one-probe), all 2.39 -> 1.67, zero misses. 4-6 MP source-resolution: Fast 2.42 / Balanced 3.42 (weak spot: oracle never bracketed below body fraction 0.25 there). Display corpus 165 cells: 1.86 -> 1.65 probes, mean bytes 262.5 -> 135.2 KB (-48%), 4-6 MP 520 -> 202 KB, rescues 5 -> 0, misses 0, one-probe 17.8% -> 35.4%. Gates: lib 381/381 serial, perceptual_api 11/11, metric_identity 3/3, CLI 12/12, all targets build.

### Opus subagent. Resampled display encodes now verify the floor against the ORIGINAL source: EncodeContext carries metric_reference (the un-resampled view) set by prepared_context() in encode/mod.rs; the search builds StreamEvaluator::for_target(context.metric_source(), ..) so the original is conditioned into the display box and candidates (decoded at the resampled/metric size) are scored through score_display_sized_candidate. last_achieved_score() (thread-local) exposes the encoder's winning score; display_resample_bench asserts encoder == reader-visible score within 1e-6 on all 22 rows (max gap before 0.05, now 0.00). New test resampled_display_encode_scores_the_original_exactly. linear_row fast path shared by fill_linear_from_view and box_downscale_view cut both full-source passes ~35% (box downscale 63 -> 41 ms on 6 MP). Net cost of the exact floor ~+3% encode time; bytes +0.015%; decode unchanged. resampled/source-res: bytes 0.458x, encode 0.276x, decode 0.328x. Gates: lib 381/381 serial, all integration targets (perceptual_api 12), CLI 12/12, all targets build. Left: evaluator rebuilds the conditioned reference (45 ms) although box_downscale_view computed the same planes; sharing them would cost the bit-exact identity.

### Opus subagent, small-image encoding. Profile (release, 7 photos box-downscaled to 64x48..640x480): JP2 boxes 85 B + main header 78-96 B are already minimal; decomposition levels already shrink (loosening the LL>=16 rule was worse, reverted); rayon spin-up and tile policy are not costs; perceptual time is T1 + reconstruct + ssimulacra2 + evaluator construction. Fixes: 256-entry sRGB->linear LUT replacing powf per sample (bit-exact; evaluator_new -32%, score_decoded -27%, 640x480 display encode -16%; perceptual encodes 5-15% faster with identical bytes), e-ink luma fold before resampling, sources below the metric's 8x8 floor resolve to Lossless instead of failing, aggregated profile scopes. Opt-in resample-to-display source path: DisplayProfile.resample_source / resampling_source(), encoded_size(), RESAMPLE_MIN_FACTOR 1.25, downscale in linear light (sRGB-space averaging failed the reader-visible floor by 0.25), CLI --resample, StreamEvaluator::score_display_sized_candidate for reader-view verification. Floor 70 into e-ink 600x450, 11 photos: resampled/source-res bytes 0.46x, encode 0.25x, decode 0.31x, probes unchanged, minimum reader-visible score 71.2 (4-6 MP: 285 KB/1.5 s -> 74 KB/0.16 s). Caveat: in the resampled path the encoder's own floor is verified against the resampled source; reader-visible floor holds empirically (min margin 1.2). Combined-tree gates: lib 381/381 serial, all integration targets, CLI 12/12, all targets build warning-free, fmt clean, cargo check -p lege ok.

### Session 8c tuning from the oracle sweep (12 full-grid + 7 Q50-screen sources, ssimulacra2-jpxl-1). Byte-cheapest outer quantizer depends on target, not source: q60 at 80, q60-75 at 85-90, q50 at 95 (all-pass ceiling 95.3-96.5), q70-75 at 97.5, q85+ at 98+; q99 never cheapest (q95 already scores 100 all-pass). Fixed [75,90,99] cost +24% bytes at 80, +6% at 95. Production now uses outer_rungs_for_target (5 target bands). Also fixed a pre-existing inner PCRD navigation failure: the loss-domain crossing fit crept <1%/probe from just under target when the feasible side was the far ceiling, exhausting Fast/Balanced budgets and shipping the ceiling stream (20240501_110934 at 80 emitted 1,012,985 bytes on the old ladder); MIN_BRACKET_STEP=1.05 forces a minimum relative climb. After: 192515 t80 107,222 B (was 452,663 new ladder / lucky 104,607 old), 110934 t80 211,876 B (was 1,012,985), t90 219,530 / 341,200 B. Lib 375/375 serial; all integration targets green; encode::ssim_dwt counter test races under parallel runner (pre-existing, papercut logged).

### Search: (1) safe_ceiling_for_rung skips the all-pass ceiling probe when the target sits >=1.5 below the corpus-minimum ceiling of the rung (q50 95.3, q60 96.5, q70 97.4, q75 97.7, q85 98.1, q90 98.3, q92 98.9, q95 99.9), seeding the first aim from the estimate; (2) after a rung wins, a finer rung is tried only with >=3 evaluations left. On 20240502_192515 target 80, Fast now emits the same 107,645 B stream as Balanced in 4 probes with no ceiling probe; 110934 target 80 209,903 B; targets 90: 219,251 / 352,381 B. Unified scale: PerceptualTarget::for_quality(q, effort) defines quality q as a SSIMULACRA2 floor of q (100 stays lossless); CLI accepts 'qN --effort fast|balanced|quality' and routes through it; --ssimulacra2 remains the explicit-score form. Calibration of the legacy open-loop Quality(q) ladder on the eight 0.8 MP corpus photos (ssimulacra2-jpxl-1, median): q10 -63.9, q30 -49.5, q50 -8.8, q60 13.4, q70 35.7, q80 52.3, q90 60.8, q95 79.7 (1.6 bpp), q99 100 (20 bpp). The legacy ladder is therefore not on the unified scale: it is far coarser than the perceptual path below q95 (perceptual score 80 needs a median 1.5 bpp, Quality(80) spends 0.77 bpp) and jumps 12x in bytes between q95 and q99. Re-pointing Quality(q) at the unified scale (bpp prior per target from the sweep: t80 1.52, t85 1.96, t90 2.60, t95 4.26, t97.5 7.08 median bpp) changes every consumer's file sizes and is left for an explicit decision. 4-6 MP calibration run still in flight at record time. Lib 375/375 serial, all integration targets and CLI unit tests green.

### Opus subagent, lege-process. Flow: page rasters are Lanczos-resized to the device preset before region cropping (pdf_tokio_pipeline.rs ~686-760), so region pixel size is the device placement box; PDF placement (pdf_artifact.rs CTM) is decoupled from XObject pixel size. New EncodingSettings::Jp2Display { max_width, max_height, floor, fallback_quality } with or_legacy(): verified display target (jp2lam EncodeOptions::display_photo with DisplayProfile eink/tablet by channel count, resampling_source) only when the source is meaningfully larger than the box, legacy ApproxQuality preset otherwise. quality_policy floors: region 78/75/70, gray overlay 70/65, full-page base 60/55 (65 measured +3..52% bytes there). All five JP2 sites declare a box; preserved-MRC path untouched. --jp2-debug rewritten to compare legacy vs floor with reader-visible SSIMULACRA2. Real 2663x4506 book-scan pages into 709x1200 e-ink box: bytes 0.68x, encode 0.38x, decode 0.23x, score equal or better. Box == source (472x800 crops): the 1+1 display controller overshoots 10-25 points at 1.1-2.0x bytes vs legacy, hence or_legacy; forwarded to the navigation agent. Gates: cargo check -p lege ok, cargo test -p lege 339+19 passed, jp2lam untouched. Remaining upstream win: encode regions from the pre-resize raster so jp2lam does the downscale inside the rate loop (pipeline restructure).

### Round 5 (no subagents): or_legacy removed and JP2 regions rendered 2x for in-loop downscale. Finding: the product renders pages AT device height (source_render_height == target_height unless slow OCR) and the planned path renders region products at crop size, so box == source is the common case and or_legacy sent nearly every JP2 region to legacy q50, which measured SSIMULACRA2 -25..42 on 21 device-resolution Central Park figure crops (median ~10). jp2lam root cause at box == source: the display policy (2-probe cap, display reserve) applied to a profile that conditions nothing; on the crops it shipped fat first probes (floor 55 landed 65-82 at up to 1.56x plain bytes). Fix: DisplayProfile::conditions(); prepared_context plans an identity profile as the plain target (resampled encodes keep theirs to condition the original reference). Crops now byte-identical to plain (21/21). lege-process: or_legacy deleted, every JP2 site verified (fallback_quality kept for encode failure only); slow-OCR hi-res raster crops feed JP2 regions/cover with the device box; planned path renders JP2 regions at JP2_REGION_RENDER_SCALE=2 so jp2lam box-filters in linear light inside the rate loop. Central Park p20-40: JPX bytes legacy 403K -> verified 965K (floor 55 vs q50, quality-level change) -> 2x render 823K (0.85x) at equal verified score; wall 3.6 s -> 4.8 s for 21 pages. Page-level jp2-debug 2800 vs 1400 render into the 1400 box: 0.85-0.90x bytes, score delta within +-1.5, encode ms 1.24-1.52x. ### Detector limit_side 1280 beats 960 and 1600 for PP-OCRv6 on wgpu

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.evidence.det-limit-side-sweep-20260822/1`

Embedded PP-OCRv6 small on the wgpu path, reading lege-process/page_0002-original.png (961x1400) against a hand transcription: limit 960 scored CER 0.25% / WER 2.81% in 7.28s, limit 1280 scored CER 0.25% / WER 2.41% in 8.31s, limit 1600 scored CER 0.31% / WER 3.21% in 8.23s. 1280 ships. 1600 exceeds the page's own long side so no resize happens, and it scores worst, indicating the downscale suppresses scan noise. The margin is about one word on 249, and the page's 1400px long side means this cannot speak to 300 DPI input; residual errors are dominated by lost inter-word spaces at a scan shading boundary, which every cap shares.

### Dropping isolated specks before glyph matching removes 18 percent of occurrences and 7 percent of bytes on the crusades scan

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.evidence.glyphfont-speck-filter-crusades-20260906/1`

PageAnalysis::of now drops a component that is grain: at most dpi^2/24000 ink pixels anywhere (2 at 240 dpi, cjb2's own 3 at 300), or at most dpi^2/4800 pixels (12 at 240) when it is no more than a quarter the page's upper-quartile component side and has no other ink within dpi/20 pixels of its box. Before: 224855 occurrences, 13087 shapes, 2.17 MB font, 2.56 MB PDF, 14.7 s. After: 184452 occurrences, 40403 specks dropped, 13060 shapes, 2.12 MB font, 2.38 MB PDF, 10.4 s. Full stops and tittles survive on page 20. The one-off shapes that dominate the font are not specks: of 11122 shapes used once, 5164 are letter-sized (17-64 px) unmatched impressions and 5782 are 4-16 px fragments, against 472 reused letter-sized prototypes.

### Generic JBIG2 costs 0.6% over sym-unify on an 886-page scan

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem.evidence.jbig2-generic-default-costs-little-20260906/1` · scope `path "lege-process/**"`

886 pages of a 240-dpi library scan, debug-fast build. Bit-exact generic region: 41 s, 21,322,267 bytes. Symbol substitution with unification: 42 s, 21,200,663 bytes — 0.6% smaller. On the first 41 pages the gap was 1.9% (894,969 against 878,208 bytes), and the plain symbol dictionary landed between the two at 879,231. ### Surface recycling and gated image-row fan-out: 2.2-4.8x per page, byte-identical, throughput neutral

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.evidence.renderer-surface-and-image-rows-2026-09-04/1`

Tenth renderer pass, measured by interleaved A/B against a binary built from a worktree of the parent commit, minimum of four batches per arm. Per-page: jpeg scan at sweep scale 87.0 -> 38.8 ms (2.24x), bilevel SAT 72.5 -> 15.0 ms (4.82x), bilevel SAT with text 59.1 -> 12.8 ms (4.61x), MRC 10.2 -> 2.8 ms (3.69x), RGB8 area-min with vector 29.1 -> 7.6 ms (3.84x), CMYK area-min with paths 271.1 -> 109.3 ms (2.48x); latin text, vector and mesh pages neutral. Two causes, both outside the per-pixel arithmetic the nine prior passes had already squeezed: a 170 MB page buffer past glibc's 32 MiB mmap threshold cost a kernel page-zero on every render (fresh alloc and fill 52 ms, reused 3.4 ms), and BilevelIntegral::build was 44 of 52 ms on a bilevel scan. The negative result is load-bearing: unconditional row fan-out cost 31% of whole-document throughput on a 640-page scan (4702 -> 6019 ms) because 13 render workers plus a 20-thread rayon pool oversubscribe the machine, so fan-out is gated on a PAGES_IN_FLIGHT guard and whole-document is neutral (median 4786 -> 4784 ms over 14 runs an arm). Output byte-identical: 148 of 148 pages across 70 documents. 193 pdf-render-cpu tests pass, including a new gate asserting the parallel SAT fill matches the retained serial walk element for element across block boundaries.

### Structures.pdf direct Arc output versus owned Vec control

`verified` · `@lege-ecosystem-perf.evidence.structures-direct-vs-owned-output-2026-08-09/3`

A corrected 21-run control temporarily restored the former packed owned-raster plus Vec-to-Arc path. It measured 196.892 ms median JPX (p25/p75 192.961/205.569), versus 204.616 ms (195.466/233.428) for direct Arc output in a sequential same-session comparison. Direct output was about 3.9% slower at the median, and the distributions overlap, so this run demonstrates no throughput improvement. Both output hashes were fdc3994f80330ee0. The direct path still removes one full-image allocation and copy; the temporary control branch was removed after measurement. Revision 1 used the native-planar fallback as its control and is superseded by this corrected packed-path measurement.

**supersedes** `@lege-ecosystem-perf.evidence.structures-direct-vs-owned-output-2026-08-09/2`
